blocks.title: Ustad ki baat
blocks.text: Pichhle page par humne dekha ke origin se guzarne wali do lines ki joint equation mein har term degree 2 ka hota hai. Aaj is qisam ki equation ko naam denge, homogeneous equation, us ki aam shakal \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) likhenge, aur Theorem 8 mein saabit karenge ke yeh HAMESHA origin se guzarne wali do lines hoti hain. Saath hi ek aasaan test seekhenge jo bata deta hai ke lines real aur alag hain, ek doosre par chadhi hui (coincident) hain, ya imaginary. Aakhir mein Example 16 mein lines ko alag alag nikalna seekhenge.

Ek equation \(f(x, y) = 0\), jo do variables \(x\) aur \(y\) mein ho, degree \(n\) (positive integer) ki homogeneous equation kehlati hai agar function \(f(x, y)\) degree \(n\) ka homogeneous ho, yani har real number \(k\) ke liye \(f(kx, ky) = k^{n}f(x, y)\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein yeh definition ka jumla ulajh gaya hai ('Let ... be any equation ... is called' dono ek saath), aur aakhir mein 'for some real number \(k\)' (kisi ek \(k\) ke liye) likha hai. Sahi baat 'har real number \(k\) ke liye' hai. Wajah: kisi ek \(k\) ke liye to har function chal jata hai, kyunke \(k = 1\) rakhein to dono taraf \(f(x, y)\) hi aata hai. Upar hum ne sahi jumla likha hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Saada alfaaz mein: \(x\) ki jagah \(kx\) aur \(y\) ki jagah \(ky\) rakhiye. Agar poori expression sirf \(k^{n}\) se multiply ho kar wapas aa jaye, to woh degree \(n\) ki homogeneous hai. Yeh tab hota hai jab har term ki total degree barabar \(n\) ho. Total degree ka matlab: \(x\) aur \(y\) ki powers ka jama; jaise \(xy\) ki degree \(1 + 1 = 2\). Misaal: \(x^{2} + 3xy\) degree 2 ki homogeneous hai, lekin \(x^{2} + 3y\) nahi, kyunke terms ki degrees 2 aur 1 hain. Isay aise samjhiye jaise photo ko zoom karna: har cheez ek hi tanasub (ratio) se badi hoti hai, shakal nahi badalti.

Misaal ke taur par, upar wali equation (v) mein \(x\) ki jagah \(kx\) aur \(y\) ki jagah \(ky\) rakhein to:
\[f(kx, ky) = k^{2}y^{2} - k^{2}(m_{1}+m_{2})xy\]
\[+\, k^{2}m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}\]
\[= k^{2}[y^{2} - (m_{1}+m_{2})xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}]\]
\[\Rightarrow f(kx, ky) = k^{2}f(x, y)\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab mein bracket ka aakhri term \(m_{1}m_{2}x^{3}\) chhapa hai aur bracket ke baad '\(= 0\)' bhi likha hai. Dono ghalat hain. Equation (v) mein \(m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}\) hai (power 2, kyunke har term degree 2 ka hai), aur bracket khud \(f(x, y)\) hai, zero nahi. Sahi line yeh hai:
\[= k^{2}[y^{2} - (m_{1}+m_{2})xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}]\]
\[\Rightarrow f(kx, ky) = k^{2}f(x, y)\]
Upar humne yahi sahi shakal likhi hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Chaliye ek aam si expression par yeh test chala kar dekhte hain: \(f(x, y) = x^{2} - 5xy + 6y^{2}\).
\[f(kx, ky) = k^{2}x^{2} - 5k^{2}xy + 6k^{2}y^{2}\]
\[= k^{2}(x^{2} - 5xy + 6y^{2}) = k^{2}f(x, y)\]
To yeh degree 2 ki homogeneous hai. Ab \(g(x, y) = x^{2} + 3y\) lijiye: \(g(kx, ky) = k^{2}x^{2} + 3ky\). Yahan poori expression se ek hi power ka \(k\) bahar nahi nikalta, kyunke pehle term mein \(k^{2}\) hai aur doosre mein sirf \(k\). Is liye \(g\) homogeneous nahi. Seedha usool: sab terms ki degree barabar ho to homogeneous, warna nahi.

Har term se \(k^{2}\) bahar aa gaya, to (v) degree 2 ki homogeneous equation hai. Aam (general) second degree homogeneous equation is tarah likhi jati hai: \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\), bashart-e-ke \(a\), \(h\) aur \(b\) teenon ek saath zero na hon.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Sawal mein se \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) kaise parhein: \(a\) = \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient, \(b\) = \(y^{2}\) ka coefficient, aur \(h\) = \(xy\) ke coefficient ka AADHA. Misaal: \(3x^{2} - 10xy + 3y^{2} = 0\) mein \(a = 3\), \(2h = -10\) is liye \(h = -5\), aur \(b = 3\). Sign hamesha number ke saath copy karna hai. 'Teenon zero na hon' wali shart sirf is liye hai ke warna equation \(0 = 0\) ban jati hai, jis ka koi matlab nahi.

Theorem 8: Har homogeneous second degree equation
\[ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0 \quad \text{...(1)}\]
origin se guzarne wali lines ka ek jora represent karti hai. Yeh lines

items: (i) real aur alag alag (distinct) hain, agar \(h^{2} > ab\)
(ii) real aur coincident (ek doosre par chadhi hui, yani asal mein ek hi line) hain, agar \(h^{2} = ab\)
(iii) imaginary (jo graph par nazar nahi aatin) hain, agar \(h^{2} < ab\)

blocks.text:
Proof: (1) ko \(b\) se multiply kar ke terms ko tarteeb dete hain:
\[b^{2}y^{2} + 2bhxy + abx^{2} = 0\]
\[b^{2}y^{2} + 2bhxy + h^{2}x^{2} - h^{2}x^{2} + abx^{2} = 0\]
\[(by + hx)^{2} - x^{2}(h^{2} - ab) = 0\]
\[\left(by + hx + x\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)\times\]
\[\left(by + hx - x\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Proof mein har line par kya hua, aaraam se dekhte hain:
1. \(b\) se multiply kiya taa ke \(y^{2}\) wala term \(b^{2}y^{2} = (by)^{2}\) ban jaye, yani poora square. Is par hum aage imaarat khari karenge.
2. \(h^{2}x^{2}\) jama bhi kiya aur minus bhi; kul farq zero, equation wahi rahi. Yeh completing the square (poora square banana) hai: \(b^{2}y^{2} + 2bhxy + h^{2}x^{2} = (by + hx)^{2}\), bilkul \((p + q)^{2} = p^{2} + 2pq + q^{2}\) ki tarah.
3. Bache hue do terms: \(-h^{2}x^{2} + abx^{2} = -x^{2}(h^{2} - ab)\), \(x^{2}\) common nikal kar.
4. Ab yeh do squares ka farq hai: \(P^{2} - Q^{2} = (P + Q)(P - Q)\), jahan \(P = by + hx\) aur \(Q = x\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\). Is formula se do linear factors mil gaye, yani do lines.
Dhyan dein: proof mein \(b \ne 0\) farz kiya gaya hai (pehle \(b\) se multiply kiya, phir lines mein \(b\) se divide hota hai). Agar \(b = 0\) ho to (1) seedha \(x(ax + 2hy) = 0\) ban jati hai: lines \(x = 0\) aur \(ax + 2hy = 0\), dono phir bhi origin se guzarti hain.

Is tarah equation (1) un do lines ka jora hai jin ki equations yeh hain:
\[by + x\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(2)}\]
aur
\[by + x\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(3)}\]

Saaf zahir hai ke lines (2) aur (3): (i) real aur alag hain agar \(h^{2} > ab\), (ii) real aur coincident hain agar \(h^{2} = ab\), (iii) imaginary hain agar \(h^{2} < ab\). Dilchasp baat yeh hai ke lines imaginary hon tab bhi woh ek real point, yani \((0, 0)\), par milti hain, kyunke yeh point joint equation (1) ko satisfy karta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(h^{2} - ab\) ka sign hi sab kuch kyun tay karta hai? Kyunke yeh square root ke andar baitha hai.
Agar \(h^{2} - ab > 0\): root ek real, non-zero number hai, to (2) aur (3) do mukhtalif real lines hain.
Agar \(h^{2} - ab = 0\): root zero hai, to (2) aur (3) dono ek hi line \(by + hx = 0\) ban jati hain (coincident).
Agar \(h^{2} - ab < 0\): negative ka square root real nahi hota, to koi real line nahi banti; sirf point \((0, 0)\) equation (1) ko satisfy karta hai.
Yeh wahi test hai jo quadratic equation ka discriminant \(B^{2} - 4AC\) karta hai. Slopes ki equation \(bm^{2} + 2hm + a = 0\) mein \(B^{2} - 4AC = 4h^{2} - 4ab = 4(h^{2} - ab)\). Pichhli classes ka purana dost naye kapron mein!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(x^{2} + xy + y^{2} = 0\) kaisi lines hain? Pehle \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) likhiye.
Jawab: \(a = 1\), \(h = 1/2\), \(b = 1\); \(h^{2} - ab = 1/4 - 1 < 0\), is liye imaginary lines; graph par sirf origin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Teeno haalaton ki ek ek misaal, taa ke test haath mein baith jaye:
1. \(x^{2} - 4y^{2} = 0\): yahan \(a = 1\), \(h = 0\), \(b = -4\). \(h^{2} - ab = 0 + 4 = 4 > 0\), to do real aur alag lines. Waqai \((x - 2y)(x + 2y) = 0\), yani \(x = 2y\) aur \(x = -2y\).
2. \(x^{2} - 4xy + 4y^{2} = 0\): \(a = 1\), \(h = -2\), \(b = 4\). \(h^{2} - ab = 4 - 4 = 0\), to coincident lines. Waqai yeh \((x - 2y)^{2} = 0\) hai, yani ek hi line \(x - 2y = 0\) do dafa.
3. \(x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 0\): \(a = 1\), \(h = 0\), \(b = 4\). \(h^{2} - ab = -4 < 0\), to imaginary lines. Waqai do squares ka jama sirf tab zero hota hai jab dono zero hon, yani sirf point \((0, 0)\).
Dekha aap ne? Sirf ek chhota sa hisaab \(h^{2} - ab\) humein bata deta hai ke graph par kya nazar aayega, factorize kiye baghair.

blocks.title: Example 16
blocks.problem: Find an equation of each of the lines represented by \(3x^{2} - 10xy + 3y^{2} = 0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(3x^{2} - 10xy + 3y^{2} = 0\), yeh homogeneous second degree equation hai.
Maloom karna: dono lines ki alag alag equations.
Tareeqa: left side ko middle term split kar ke factorize karenge. Homogeneous quadratic bilkul \(3t^{2} - 10t + 3\) ki tarah factor hoti hai. Har factor ko zero rakhne se ek line milti hai (zero-product rule). Yeh tareeqa is liye theek hai ke joint equation asal mein do lines ka product hi to hai; hum bas woh product wapas khol rahe hain.

Pehle dekh lein ke lines real hain
\[a = 3,\quad 2h = -10 \Rightarrow h = -5,\quad b = 3\]
\[h^{2} - ab = 25 - 9 = 16 > 0\]
Kyun: Theorem 8 kehta hai \(h^{2} > ab\) ho to do real aur alag lines. Yani real factors zaroor milenge. Aur 16 perfect square hai, is liye factors ke coefficients poore numbers honge; split karna aasan rahega.
Dhyan dein: \(h\) \(xy\) ke coefficient ka AADHA hai: \(-10\) nahi, \(-5\).

Middle term ko split karein
\[3x^{2} - 9xy - xy + 3y^{2} = 0\]
Kyun: aise do numbers chahiye jin ka product \(3 \times 3 = 9\) ho aur jama \(-10\). Woh \(-9\) aur \(-1\) hain. Is liye \(-10xy\) ko \(-9xy - xy\) likh diya; value wohi rahi, sirf shakal badli.

Jore bana kar common nikalein
\[3x(x - 3y) - y(x - 3y) = 0\]
Kyun: pehle do terms mein \(3x\) common hai aur aakhri do mein \(-y\). Dono jore same bracket \((x - 3y)\) chhorte hain; yahi nishani hai ke split sahi hua.

Factorize karein
\[(x - 3y)(3x - y) = 0\]
Kyun: ab \((x - 3y)\) dono hisson mein common hai, use bahar nikal liya.

Lines alag karein
\[x - 3y = 0 \quad \text{aur} \quad 3x - y = 0\]
Kyun: product zero hai to koi ek factor zero hoga. Har factor origin se guzarne wali ek line hai (dono mein constant term nahi).

Tasdeeq:
\[(x - 3y)(3x - y) = 3x^{2} - xy - 9xy + 3y^{2}\]
\[= 3x^{2} - 10xy + 3y^{2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: multiply kar ke asal equation wapas aa gayi. Slopes \(1/3\) aur \(3\) hain: jama \(10/3 = -2h/b\) aur product \(1 = a/b\), bilkul jaise 5.9 mein aayega.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Agar middle term aasaani se split ho jaye to factorize kijiye, yeh sab se tez hai. Agar na ho (surds aa rahe hon ya \(\sec\alpha\) jaise letters hon) to seedha tayyar lines (2) aur (3) istemal kijiye: \(by + x(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = 0\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f(x, y) = 0\) degree \(n\) ki homogeneous hai jab \(f(kx, ky) = k^{n}f(x, y)\); yani har term ki degree \(n\).
2. Aam shakal: \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\); \(h\) = \(xy\) ke coefficient ka aadha.
3. Theorem 8: yeh hamesha origin se guzarne wali do lines hain: \(h^{2} > ab\) real aur alag, \(h^{2} = ab\) coincident, \(h^{2} < ab\) imaginary.
4. Lines: \(by + x(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = 0\), ya seedha dono factors.
5. Imaginary lines bhi real point \((0, 0)\) par milti hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(xy\) ka poora coefficient \(h\) le lena: \(3x^{2} - 10xy + 3y^{2}\) mein \(h = -5\) hai, \(-10\) nahi.
2. Negative \(h\) ya \(b\) ka sign gira dena; sign hamesha number ke saath likhiye.
3. Middle term split karte waqt product \(ab\) ki jagah sirf \(a\) ya sirf \(b\) dekhna.
